### rodaddy — 2026-08-03T16:28:19Z

## Corpus map + purpose (operator, 2026-08-03)

**Why this corpus matters (operator's words, distilled):** Kevin's mode of working with the agents is exactly what Open Brain exists to fix — agents that knew the code but answered every question as confident idiots from empty recall. An agent in one of these repos should have all repo information present and RESEARCH questions, never spit back unresearched recall. The Skippy<->Kevin threads are the record of that working relationship and its corrections.

**Discord corpus, precise:** King Capital server -> **King Dev** channel -> sub-threads: **fixed dashboard**, **king dashboard**, **king signals**, **temp signal backtest**. Most of the conversations live there. Extraction should pull LARGE CHUNKS (whole-thread exports) — the back-and-forth is the value, so no per-message cherry-picking at ingest time; distillation happens downstream in the candidate pipeline.

**Backups verdict, corrected after a deep second sweep:** raw Discord logs are NOT in /Volumes/collab/agent-backups — but `agents/skippy/assets/hermes/memories/` DOES hold Skippy's own distilled `MEMORY.md` + `USER.md` (~23K) and the full runtime logic (plugins/gateway/cron). Those memory files are immediate, high-density seed candidates in their own right and are probably the "found in the backups" recollection. So the adapter has THREE inputs, in value order:
1. Discord thread exports (King Dev + the four sub-threads) — the raw back-and-forth, includes Kevin's side.
2. Skippy's distilled memories from the backup (small, curated, ingestable today without any new adapter).
3. Hermes-side runtime annotations, only if the bilby live store adds anything (check once, read-only).

Kevin-facing outcome this feeds: the seeded repos (king-signals, king-dashboard, etc. — #520 receipts) plus the promoted Skippy/Kevin guidance become the startup context for the cc-* box rollout (#500 §1), so Kevin's agents stop answering from nothing.

### rodaddy — 2026-08-03T16:31:47Z

## CORPUS FOUND (RUNNING-verified 2026-08-03, read-only)

The operator was right: the full Hermes conversation store exists, on Skippy's own box — `skippy@10.71.20.111:~/.hermes/` (1.6G total):

| store | size | sessions | messages |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles/king-capital/state.db` | 154M | 168 | **6,227** |
| `state.db` (default profile) | 705M | 375 | **18,827** |

SQLite, with FTS indexes already built. Schema verified read-only:
- `messages`: id, session_id, **role, content**, tool_call_id, **tool_calls**, tool_name, timestamp, token_count, **reasoning / reasoning_content / reasoning_details**, codex_*_items, platform_message_id, observed, active, compacted
- `sessions`: id, source, **user_id**, model, model_config, **system_prompt**, parent_session_id, started_at/ended_at, message_count, title, cwd, handoff_*, …

So this corpus is STRICTLY RICHER than a Discord API export: it carries the messages (both sides — Kevin's turns are `role=user` with `user_id`), the **system prompts per session**, tool calls, and reasoning — "all of the Hermes logic" the Discord route would have missed. The king-capital profile db is the Skippy<->Kevin working corpus (last write Jul 13); the 705M default-profile db extends through Jul 31.

**Adapter shape this settles:** SQLite -> normalized turns -> the #454 bulk-ingest SQLite staging (a natural fit — staging is already SQLite). No Discord API dependency for the primary corpus; the Discord export route (prior comment) demotes to gap-filling for anything after the last state.db write.

Next concrete step: copy the two .db files (read-only source) to `{temp_workspace}` staging on the Mac, then build the normalizer against the real schema above. Also snapshot-worthy: `~/.hermes/sessions/` (53M) and `state-snapshots/` (23M), same box, not yet inspected.
